messages:
maya: Hey team — drafting the internal announcement + release notes for the runtime rollout (runtime v1.12.3). Deploy window tonight 23:00 UTC. Can folks quick-check the blurb and the rollback wording?

maya: Draft blurb (feel free to edit inline):
```
Release: Runtime v1.12.3 rollout (hosted + dedicated) — scheduled 23:00 UTC
What: Performance and batching improvements for long-context models; bugfix for KV cache misindexing
Impact: Short canary, then gradual rollout. Most customers: no change. Some high-throughput routes may see 5-10% lower latency.
Action: Pinning will be available for enterprise customers to lock to previous runtime for 72 hours if regressions are observed. Ops will run a staged canary and monitor key eval sets and SLOs.
Rollback: If we detect a regression in the eval set or P50/P95 increases > 15% for 30m, we will pin affected customers back to v1.12.2 and abort further rollout.
Contact: @maya, @luis, @tom for runbook/rollback.
```

tom: Quick notes — please: 1) explicitly say "pinned to runtime v1.12.2" when describing rollback target, 2) call out the fallback model routing if binary rollback isn't possible.

luis: I can handle the pinning step. I've already pinned staging. Command we use: `infra pin runtime v1.12.3 --env prod --at=23:10` (will run after canary confirms).

jen: Edit suggestion: change "72 hours" to "up to 72 hours" and add a short line about customer comms for those with pinned runtimes so support has a canned response. Eg: "Customers pinned to v1.12.2 will see no change; contact support if you have questions."

sam: From rollback POV: add a runbook link and a short checklist — watch eval-set alpha/regression alerts, confirm KV-cache metrics, confirm no new errors in model-serve logs. I'll paste the checklist in a follow-up. :+1:

alexa: Also include the change window in localized times for EU/US-PT — some PMs asked. Maybe: "23:00 UTC (16:00 PT / 00:00 CET)"

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary start 1876123499 on prod-cluster-c2 by @luis. Canary id c-8934. Notifying #incidents if thresholds breached.

luis: Canary is running now. Observing traffic on canary: routing 2% -> c-8934. Initial telemetry looks good (P95 stable). Will escalate if anything spikes.

maya: Thanks — I incorporated edits. Revised blurb below (final internal copy):
```
Release: Runtime v1.12.3 rollout (hosted + dedicated) — scheduled 23:00 UTC (16:00 PT / 00:00 CET)
What: Performance and batching improvements for long-context models; bugfix for KV cache misindexing
Impact: Short canary, then gradual rollout. Most customers: no change. Some high-throughput routes may see 5-10% lower latency.
Pinning/rollback: Ops can pin customers to the previous runtime (v1.12.2) for up to 72 hours if regressions are observed. If eval-set regressions or P50/P95 increases > 15% sustained for 30m are detected, affected customers will be pinned back to v1.12.2 and rollout will be halted.
Fallbacks: When full rollback is not feasible, traffic will be routed to compatible model variants or lower-throughput tiers per routing policy.
Customer comms: Customers pinned to v1.12.2 will see no change; support should use the canned response in the runbook.
Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-rollouts
Contacts: @maya, @luis, @tom (ops)
```

tom: LGTM. Add one-line for engineering: "No schema or API changes in this release." avoids confused follow-ups.

maya: Good call. Added that line and finalised the internal announcement. I'll post to #general + email to enterprise CSMs 10m after we confirm canary. Thanks all. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary c-8934 completed at 1876123680. Metrics look within thresholds. Scheduled progressive rollout started at 1876123695.

luis: Progressive rollout proceeding. Monitoring dashboards up. I'll pin prod to v1.12.2 if any alert trips.

maya: Publishing internal note now and emailing CSMs. If anyone needs to change the wording post-send, ping me here quickly.

jen: Nice work — thanks for the quick turn-around. :thumbsup:
